Here is the revised Product Specification for "SmartDisclosure," updated to remove the login requirement for the inventor, ensuring a frictionless, immediate-start experience.

Product Specification: SmartDisclosure (Frictionless Interactive IDF)
1. Executive Summary

SmartDisclosure is an AI-powered, conversational web application designed to replace the traditional Invention Disclosure Form (IDF). It prioritizes zero-friction access, allowing inventors to immediately document ideas without creating accounts or remembering passwords. It uses Generative AI to actively listen, analyze multimodal inputs (text, audio, video, sketches), and ask real-time follow-up questions. The system compiles the session into a structured legal document accessible via a unique secure link for patent attorneys.

2. User Roles

The Inventor: The creative individual providing the information. Access is granted via a unique session token; no credentials required.

The Attorney: The legal professional reviewing the disclosure. Accesses completed forms via unique generated links.

3. Core Functional Requirements
3.1. Session Initiation (The "Zero-Login" Flow)

Landing Page: A simple, clean page with a single call to action: "Start New Invention Disclosure."

Session Token: Upon clicking start, the system generates a unique, cryptographically secure UUID (e.g., session_xyz123) in the URL.

Resume Capability: The user is provided a "Resume Link" (or the URL is bookmarked) to return to this specific session if they close the browser.

3.2. Phase I: Technical Extraction (Dynamic Follow-up)

Persona: Professional technical consultant.

Input Handling: Text, Audio (Speech-to-Text), Visuals (OCR/Vision), Video uploads.

Step 1: Identity & Context (Since no login exists)

Prompt: "Welcome. To begin, please enter your full name and work email address so we can associate this disclosure with you." (Populates PDF Header).

Prompt: "What is the proposed title of this invention?" (Ref: PDF Section 1).

Step 2: The Core Interview (Problem/Solution)

Input: Inventor dictates the technical problem.

AI Analysis: Checks for specificity.

Dynamic Follow-up: "You mentioned the system is 'more efficient.' Can you quantify that comparison against the closest related art?" (Ref: PDF Section 3).

Step 3: Enablement (The "How")

Input: Inventor uploads a system diagram.

Vision Analysis: AI identifies labeled components.

Dynamic Follow-up: "I see 'Module A' connects to the database in your drawing. Is that a wired or wireless connection, and what protocol is used?" (Ref: PDF Section 4 & 5).

Step 4: The Checkpoint

Output: "Based on our conversation, here is a summary of your invention: [AI Summary]. Is this accurate?"

3.3. Phase II: The Legal "Hard" Facts (Static Mode)

This phase covers Sections 6–13 of the PDF. The AI switches to "Form Filler" mode. It will simply present the questions and record answers verbatim without interpreting or asking follow-ups.

Inventorship: "Please list ALL inventors (including yourself), along with citizenship and residence addresses." (Ref: PDF Section 6).

Dates: "Has alpha or beta testing occurred? If so, please provide dates." (Ref: PDF Section 7).

Public Disclosure:

"Has this been shown to anyone outside the company without an NDA?" (Ref: PDF Section 12).

"Are there any upcoming trade shows or publications?" (Ref: PDF Section 13).

4. User Interface (UI) Specifications
4.1. The Inventor View

Layout: Split screen.

Left (60%): Multimedia Chat Interface. Large microphone button. Drag-and-drop zone.

Right (40%): "Live Draft Preview."

Real-time Visualization: As the inventor speaks/types, the Right Panel fills in the PDF sections (Title, Background, Description).

Session Guard: A subtle notification at the top: "Your session is auto-saved to this URL. Don't share this link until submitted."

4.2. The Attorney View (The Output)

Access: A separate, generated URL (e.g., smartIDF.com/attorney-view/submission-ID).

Dashboard:

Metadata: Submission date, Inventor Email (collected in Step 1).

Structured Disclosure: Content mapped to the Annex B headings.

Attachments: Gallery of diagrams/videos.

Raw Transcript: Collapsible view of the conversation for context.

5. Technical Process Flow

Initiation: User clicks "Start." System generates Session_ID.

Identity Collection: AI asks for Name/Email immediately (replacing login data).

Interview Loop:

User inputs multimodal data.

LLM Processing: Analyzes for "Novelty" and "Enablement."

Clarification: If vague -> Ask Follow-up.

Draft Update: Extracted facts populate the JSON structure.

Legal Phase: Linear questioning (Dates, Bars to patentability).

Submission:

User clicks "Submit."

System locks the Session_ID (preventing further edits).

System compiles data into the Attorney View format.

System emails the Attorney Access Link to the designated legal email address.

6. Sample Interaction Script

System: "Welcome. To start, please provide your Full Name and Email."
User: "Jane Doe, jane@techco.com"
System: "Thanks, Jane. What are we calling this invention?" (Ref: PDF Section 1)
User: "A self-healing concrete mix."
System: "Got it. Please describe the technical problem this addresses." (Ref: PDF Section 3)
User (Audio): "Current concrete cracks in cold weather. Ours uses bacteria to fill the cracks."
System (Analysis): Need more detail on the bacteria and the activation mechanism.
System (Follow-up): "Interesting. Which specific strain of bacteria is used? And how do they activate only when a crack forms?"
User (Text): "It uses Bacillus subtilis. It activates upon exposure to water entering the crack."
System (Confirmation): "Understood. Noted: Bacillus subtilis activated by water ingress."

7. Submission & Output Generation

Upon clicking SUBMIT:

Consolidation: The system strips the conversational pleasantries. It maps the answers to the specific headings in the Annex B PDF.

Page Generation: A unique web page is generated for this specific disclosure.

Attorney Notification:

Recipient: legal@company.com

Subject: New Disclosure Submitted: [Title]

Body: "A new invention disclosure has been submitted by [Inventor Name]. You can review the full disclosure, attachments, and transcripts at the following link: [Unique_Attorney_Link]."

8. Security Note

Since there is no login, security relies on the secrecy of the session URL.

Once "Submit" is clicked, the Inventor's edit link becomes read-only to prevent post-submission tampering.

The Attorney link should require an access code (sent separately) or simple IP whitelisting to ensure only the legal team can view the output.

**Analyzing the Core Goal**

The aim is an effortless, AI-enhanced Invention Disclosure Form web app. My focus is sharpened on the technical foundation - React 18+, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. Since my task involves reasoning and technical extraction from both text and audio, I'll use `gemini-3-flash-preview` for the primary logic while keeping `gemini-2.5-flash-latest` (or `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-09-2025` if using Live API) specifically for the audio handling. This should provide a balanced approach to both speed and accuracy.


**Optimizing Model Use**

I'm now revising my model choice strategy. Recognizing the nuances, I'm leaning towards `gemini-2.5-flash-latest` (or `gemini-2.5-flash` for short) to handle the multimodal inputs, particularly audio, due to its specialized design. While I was initially aiming for `gemini-3-flash-preview` for overall reasoning, the dedicated focus on `gemini-2.5-flash-latest` ensures optimal support for audio processing and extraction, balancing between reasoning and efficiency. This will make for a more elegant integration.

\n\n**Assembling File Structure**

I'm currently finalizing the file structure, which lays the groundwork for the user interface. I have a firm structure, which should be quick and easy to complete: `metadata.json`, `index.html`, `index.tsx`, `types.ts`, `constants.ts` (with prompt engineering), `services/geminiService.ts`, `services/storageService.ts`, `components/AudioRecorder.tsx`, and `components/ChatInterface.tsx` are all ready to go.

1. **Ask Once**: Ask the core question.
2. **Clarify (1st Strike)**: If the response is vague (e.g., "it's better", "it's faster"), ask for specific metrics or examples.
3. **Propose (2nd Strike)**: If the response is STILL vague, **generate a numbered list of 3 likely technical options** based on the context and ask the user to select or correct.
4. **Move On**: Once confirmed, update the field.

    **CURRENT PHASE: 1. BACKGROUND & PROBLEM IDENTIFICATION**
    
    GOALS:
    - Identify 'inventorName' and 'inventorEmail' (if missing).
    - Identify 'title' (short, descriptive).
    - Identify 'problem' (The specific technical deficiency in the prior art).

  `,

    - If files are uploaded, **summarize them** in 'generalOverview' and ask: "Is this a fair summary of the concept?"
    - If text is provided, summarize it and confirm.
    - **TRANSITION**: Set 'nextPhase': true ONLY when you have a confirmed 'title' and a 'generalOverview'.
    - **TRANSITION BEHAVIOR**: When setting 'nextPhase': true, simply confirm you have the overview. **DO NOT** ask about the "Problem" yet. The system will ask that automatically.
  `,

  [Phase.PROBLEM]: `
    **CURRENT PHASE: 1. PROBLEM IDENTIFICATION**
    
    GOALS:
    - Identify 'problem' (The specific technical deficiency in the prior art).

    STRATEGY:
    - You already have a 'generalOverview' from the previous phase.
    - **MANDATORY EXPLANATION**: Even if the 'generalOverview' (from Phase 0) was derived from a perfect document, you **MUST** ask the user to explain the problem in their own words at least once in this phase. Do not just rely on the document.
    - Ask: "I have the summary from your document, but in your own words, what is the specific technical deficiency or limitation in the current state of the art that makes this invention necessary?"
    - **VAGUE CHECK**: If they say "it solves latency", ask "How? Is it network latency, processing latency? Can you quantify it?"
    - **FAILSAFE**: If they fail to be specific twice, output: "I'm having trouble pinning down the problem. Is it: 1) High CPU usage, 2) Network packet loss, or 3) Storage inefficiency?"
    - **TRANSITION**: Set 'nextPhase': true ONLY when the 'problem' is clearly defined and confirmed by the user.
    - **TRANSITION BEHAVIOR**: When setting 'nextPhase': true, simply confirm the problem is clear. **DO NOT** ask about the "Solution" yet. The system will ask that automatically.
  `,

  [Phase.SOLUTION]: `
    **CURRENT PHASE: 2. DETAILED DESCRIPTION & IMPLEMENTATION**

    GOALS:
    - Identify 'solution' (The core mechanism).
    - Identify 'technicalDetails' (Deep dive into implementation).
    - Analyze 'diagramDescription' (from images).

    STRATEGY:
    1. **INITIAL OPEN-ENDED INQUIRY**: 
       - The phase starts with a broad question. Allow the user to explain the "How" in their own words first.

    2. **CLASSIFY & DRILL DOWN (SUBSEQUENT TURNS)**:
       - Once the user provides the initial explanation, classify the invention and pivot to a CUSTOMIZED line of questioning.

      A. **MECHANICAL / APPARATUS**:
         - **Components**: "What specific NEW components are added? (e.g., a specific valve, sensor, lever, or gear)."
         - **Control/Operation**: "Does this involve a control sequence? (e.g., Opening a first valve for X duration, then closing a second valve). How are these components controlled?"
         - **Structure/Geometry**: "Describe the physical shape, geometry, dimensions, and how elements interact with each other."

      B. **SOFTWARE / METHOD**:
         - **Step-by-Step**: "Walk through the process step-by-step."
         - **Data Transformation**: "At each step, what is the input? EXACTLY how is the data transformed? What is the output?"
         - **AI/ML**: "If using a Neural Network, describe the architecture (CNN, Transformer), the specific operations on the input, and how the output is generated. Do not accept 'it processes data'—ask 'what mathematical operations occur?'."
      
      C. **MATERIALS / CHEMICAL**:
         - **Composition**: "What are the ingredients, ratios, and acceptable ranges?"
         - **Principle**: "What is the chemical reaction or physical principle involved?"
         - **Process**: "What are the manufacturing parameters (Temperature, Pressure, Time)?"

    3. **ADVANTAGE & VARIATION (MANDATORY)**:
       - **Advantages**: "What is the specific technical advantage of [Novel Feature X]?"
       - **Alternatives**: "Can we generalize? Are there alternative materials, geometries, or steps that would also work?"
       - **Optional Features**: "Are there optional features that enhance performance but aren't strictly required?"

    - **TRANSITION**: Set 'nextPhase': true ONLY when you have:
      1. A clear step-by-step or structural description.
      2. Specifics (geometries, data transforms, or compositions).
      3. Technical advantages and alternatives recorded.
    - **TRANSITION BEHAVIOR**: When setting 'nextPhase': true, simply confirm the solution is recorded. **DO NOT** ask about "Legal" details yet.
  `,

  [Phase.LEGAL]: `
    **CURRENT PHASE: 3. LEGAL & FORMALITIES**

    GOALS:
    - Identify 'inventorsList' (Who else contributed?).
    - Identify 'testingDates' (When did it work?).
    - Identify 'publicDisclosures' (NDAs, papers, talks?).

    STRATEGY:
    - **ONE BY ONE**: Do not bundle these questions. Ask them sequentially.
    
    1. **Inventorship**: Ask "Who contributed to the conception of this invention? Please list all names." (Wait for answer to update 'inventorsList').
    2. **Dates**: Once inventors are confirmed, ask "When was this invention first tested or reduced to practice?" (Wait for answer to update 'testingDates').
    3. **Disclosures**: Finally, ask "Have there been any public disclosures (papers, demos, open source) or are any planned soon?" (Update 'publicDisclosures' and 'upcomingDisclosures').

    - **TRANSITION**: Set 'nextPhase': true ONLY after all 3 topics (Inventors, Dates, Disclosures) are explicitly answered.
  `
};

export const getSystemInstruction = (phase: Phase) => {
  return `${BASE_INSTRUCTION}\n\n${PHASE_INSTRUCTIONS[phase]}`;
};
